author: Reanimated
text_post: As I creep more and more towards the disgusting age of 40, I wonder what the hell I'm going to do for my birthday or if I should even give a shit anymore.  I've had very few birthday parties after college.  I usually find concerts to go to but it doesn't look like there's anything I'm interested in going to anywhere near my birthday.  I'm stuck in the northeast for way longer than expected, so that destroys the default Los Angeles plan of having my friends there just saying fuck it let's go to Disneyland and ignore all of the bullshit in the world.  I received a joint birthday party invite from one of my only single girl friends around here but it's at a Renaissance Fair and I have never been to one and I thought that was something that only high school nerds go to.  Maybe I should visit my "special escort" for an extended period of time?  What do you guys do on your birthday nowadays?  I think the responses will be interesting considering there is such a wide range of ages here.

author: AKU
text_post: When I was fifteen my mother totally forgot my birthday,  ever since birthdays (anyone's for that matter)  and holidays have no meaning for me anymore,  it's just another shit day.

author: BlackPiller2014
text_post: I don't have to wait until my Birthday to do all those things you described. In fact my mother used to suggest treating me in advance to a gift I really wanted early and then putting it down to "oh that can be your early Birthday present- yes?" So it was a neat and thoughtful way of me getting what I wanted/needed in a timely fashion and then understanding I'd pay it off at a later date. Rather than holding my breath or wishing my life away. This started with me getting a Playstation when she deposited a Bank Giro early for me. I still had to trade in my old SEGA but I got the Playstation I desired. I don't wait for exact date I've since had - Self funded holiday to Orlando Florida in a pre 9/11, 2001 (UNIVERSAL not Disney) - Had a run of hot Escorts in 2010-2011 aged 29 (before reaching the dreaded 3-0- in 2011) - Visited Museums and the like - Went to a metal festival in 2009 that was a major event for many bands there (and featured on many of their individual live DVDs sold worldwide) I get the pressure. Marketers like people to believe that Birthdays are always poolside parties, boat trips on a power-yacht etc. True some high status people do this for milestone events "sweet 16". But generally as we get older we save pestering people to come out in mass for more mature events - Engagement parties - Weddings I'd say last Birthday I gave a damn with friends around etc was - Aged 12 years old in 1993 and had a Jurassic Park themed Birthday - Age 16 years old when I was on holiday in Gumbet Turkey. Had a meal at an unofficial, unlicensed Beavis and Butthead themed restaurant before heading out on a bar crawl with my Sister and her then Boyfriend getting shit-faced.

author: cerebral_barrier
text_post: I often forget about my own birthday.   For a while, I even forgot how old I was.   I seen to have to recalculate it each year so I remember that I'm no longer 25.   Birthdays and holidays ceased to be important after my mom died. As far as what I do;  I'm usually working.

author: AKU
text_post: People ask what I do for my birthday, I tell them I do nothing it's just another day it means nothing and they say "but... blah blah blah " and I proceed to ruin their happy little illusion by telling them "you only had one ' birthday ' now all you are doing is deluding yourself because all you are actually doing is celebrating that you are one more year closer to DEATH" I'm sure I'm not the only person that says "I didn't ask to be born" especially given the shit we put up with EVERY FUCKING DAY.

author: Reanimated
text_post: Yes, you can pretty much do all of those things on a day other than your birthday.  However, would you be able to gather a group of people that cared about you to focus all of their attention on you in a certain venue for the entire day on any day besides your birthday?  I highly doubt that.  You'd be going to these events solo.  I don't mind doing most things solo but I would feel like a total loser going to a theme park myself and riding the rides by myself.  I absolutely hate engagement parties and weddings because they have given me nothing but false hope where I get invited by a girl to said events and wind up in the friend zone.  I'd love to attend a big Hollywood wedding one day even if I was just a friend.  Oh and your Jurassic Park themed birthday party sounds pretty cool especially for 12 years old.  I didn't have any friends at 12 and no recollection of what I did for my 12th birthday.  And a Beavis and Butthead themed restaurant sounds like the most fucking amazing thing ever.  I loved that show as a teen and was amped when Mike Judge brought it back again.  I'm hoping it gets resurrected yet again.  At 16, my birthday party was extremely lame, something like just me and two of my friends going out to eat.  From looking at photos and from memory, birthday parties from ages 1 through 9 all completely kicked ass and then 17 through 21 in college were pretty damn awesome.  Everything after that I think has been pretty lackluster.

author: BlackPiller2014
text_post: You interpreted correctly that I did all those activities (Florida, Metal Festival. Museums and Escorts) on my own. You probably read due to my Father's old job in the forces I had lead and got used to a solitary lifestyle growing up. Ad-hoc friendships (and enemies alike) cut short due to moving feels like those experiences never existed. Life between 17-22 was pretty shitty for me and the worst years of my life (sans the Florida holiday 2001), so at least you had that going for you. The metal festival, museums and escorts (2009-present) just shows how diverse and incompatible my palette of interests are. You'd be hard pressed to find anyone doing those combined on the regular. The Jurassic Park themed Birthday was cool correct. Mainly printed paper plates, napkins, Triceratops cake. I'd allowed it to be my last "child like Birthday"and was the last-time I collected toys. Teens try to outdo each other with when they refrained from toys but I have no regrets. The following year, anime, metal and girls were all the rage instead so I'll forgive myself for one last ride. I had friends from various periods of my life and it was the last time when I didn't "specialise" my friends based on cliques. The Beavis and Butthead restaurant (in Turkey) was not a big "theme" per-se. It had the cartoon logo out the front "Beavis and Butthead's". I had initially passed on it as a gimmick, but considering the funny name and decor of t-shirts and posters on the wall. Not to mention it was one of the few places that was sizeable, exterior and interior presentable and the proprietors didn't bug you for business as you passed; I gave it a crack on my Birthday with my Sister and her then boyfriend in tow. The food and drink were all based on the show and actually well done. I recall I had Nachos with Cheese (and Mediterranean Salad) and Cherryade cocktail as part of my Birthday lunch. Can't find any images other than this from a travel log from 2006 with the B&B plate mats.

author: cerebral_barrier
text_post: Now that you mention it,  that's exactly what I do. Nothing is particularly important to me  and my sense of purpose ended with my mother's life.   I've been psychologically "drifting" ever since she passed; using raw logic to guild me through life.     This logic helps me differentiate between what people believe and what really is but as a side-effect, I am now so self-aware now that I can no longer see or participate in the illusion of life.   I now have no real desires, ambitions or goals; they simply don't interest me anymore.

author: Laplacian
text_post: I haven’t had a birthday party, wherein people I have a mutual trust and association spend time with me socially to commemorate the anniversary of my escape from the womb, since I was in high school. Usually I get a few texts from people I don’t care much for, and at work they give a thing of popcorn (I hate popcorn). Other than that, it’s basically a regular day.

author: BrickInWall
text_post: I usually plan a meal out with my male friends. My ex-gf always insisted on the whole party shebang which I never really liked. Us five guys (the same crew as the roadtrips) in a meaty restaurant with plenty of beer shooting the shit and discussing recent breakups is much preferable to any forced "ooh, we're having fun, haven't we, dear" at home with female guest (have to cut on burps and non-PC remarks) and the prying eyes of the Ex, who's liable to keep nagging for days on any perceived break of etiquette on my part.
